issues.legal_issue: A decree awarding owelty in a partition creates a charge on the property allotted to the co-sharer liable to pay it, even without an express declaration, and that charge takes priority over earlier encumbrances.
material_facts: A partition decree allocated properties of unequal values among co-sharers and directed the representative of one branch to pay another co-sharer money to equalize their shares.
The decree directed that the payment be made from the property allotted to the paying branch, but did not expressly declare a charge over that property.
The recipient sought payment from the proceeds of property allotted to the paying branch, while another creditor claimed rights arising from earlier enforcement steps.
issues.conclusion: The owelty award created a charge by necessary implication on the property allotted to the paying branch, and the charge had priority over prior encumbrances.
issues.legal_principle: A partition court may award owelty to equalize unequal allotments, and the recipient has a lien or charge on the allotment made to the payer even if the decree does not expressly declare one. That charge takes precedence over earlier mortgages or other liens. The Court relied on Shahebzada Mohommed Kazim Shah v. R. S. Hill and Poovanalingam Servai v. Veerai, as well as the stated principles in texts on equity, cotenancy, and partition.

rule.if: partition_proceeding and unequal_property_allotments and compensatory_payment_awarded_to_co_sharer and property_allotted_to_payer and not express_charge_declared

predicates.partition_proceeding: The dispute arises from a proceeding to divide jointly held property among co-sharers.
predicates.unequal_property_allotments: The property allotted to the co-sharers differs in value, leaving their shares unequal without an adjustment.
predicates.compensatory_payment_awarded_to_co_share: The decree directs one co-sharer to pay another money to equalize their shares.
predicates.property_allotted_to_payer: The property subject to the payment obligation is allotted to the co-sharer required to pay.
predicates.express_charge_declared: The decree expressly declares a charge on the property to secure the payment.

issues.definition: When a partition proceeding awards a co-sharer an equalizing payment from property allotted to the payer, the payment is secured by a charge on that property even if the decree does not expressly declare one, and that charge has priority over earlier encumbrances.

issues.legal_issue: An insolvency receiver cannot recover money paid or deposited in compliance with an operative decree directing payment to a co-sharer when the decree has not been varied or reversed.
material_facts: An operative partition decree directed the insolvency receiver to pay money to a co-sharer as part of the adjustment of shares.
The receiver made payments and deposited money in court in compliance with the decree.
The decree was not varied or reversed, but the receiver later sought repayment and withdrawal of the deposit after a court had rejected the claim that the decree expressly created a charge.
issues.conclusion: The receiver was not entitled to recover the payments or withdraw the deposit; the applications for restitution were dismissed and the beneficiary was entitled to the deposited amount.
issues.legal_principle: The majority held that the payment was properly made under the partition decree and the implied owelty charge. In his separate opinion, Sarkar J. considered the operative decree independently sufficient: the receiver was bound to comply with it, and whether a charge or another priority existed did not permit recovery while the decree stood. He stated that section 144 of the Code of Civil Procedure applies to payments under a decree that has been varied or reversed, which had not occurred. He also distinguished a creditor of the insolvency estate, who may receive a dividend, from a beneficiary holding a decree against the receiver. Sarkar J. further considered that the earlier decision did not operate as res judicata between the beneficiary and the receiver on an issue that was neither between them nor necessary to the earlier relief.

rule.if: receiver_restitution_proceeding and operative_decree_directs_payment_to_claimant and receiver_paid_or_deposited_under_decree and not decree_varied_or_reversed

predicates.receiver_restitution_proceeding: An insolvency receiver applies to recover money paid or deposited for a decree beneficiary.
predicates.operative_decree_directs_payment_to_clai: A decree that remains in force directs payment to the person from whom repayment is sought or for whose benefit the deposit was made.
predicates.receiver_paid_or_deposited_under_decree: The receiver made the payment or deposit in compliance with that decree.
predicates.decree_varied_or_reversed: A court has varied or reversed the decree under which the receiver paid or deposited the money.

issues.definition: If an insolvency receiver seeks recovery of money paid or deposited in compliance with a decree that remains in force and directs payment to the claimant, the receiver's recovery claim must be rejected.
